rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Moses account follows Midian because their eras were close and the prophets closely connected; Moses preached during Shuayb's life and married his daughter.
rows.anchor: وعقبت قصة مدين بذكر بعثة موسى عليه السلام لقرب ما بين زمنيهما ، ولشدة الصلة بين النبيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle qad strengthens the report, as it does the report about Noah in 11:25.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر ب ( قد ) مثل تأكيد خبر نوح عليه السلام في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in bi-āyātinā means accompaniment: the signs accompanied Moses's mission throughout his invitation to Pharaoh and his council.
rows.anchor: فإن ظهور الآيات كان مصاحبا لزمن الإرسال إلى فرعون وهو مدة دعوة موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulṭān means a clear proof that demonstrates its bearer is truthful, whether a rational argument or divine support.
rows.anchor: والسلطان : البرهان المبين ، أي المظهر صدق الجائي به وهو الحجة العقلية أو التأييد الإلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immediate mention of Pharaoh's followers obeying him after Moses's mission implies Pharaoh ordered them to deny the message.
rows.anchor: ففهم منه أن فرعون أمرهم بتكذيب تلك الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating Pharaoh's name instead of a pronoun publicizes his blame and the fact that his command lacked right guidance.
rows.anchor: وإظهار اسم فرعون في المرة الثانية دون الضمير والمرة الثالثة للتشهير بهم ، والإعلان بذمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause denying that Pharaoh's command was rightly guided is circumstantial to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وما أمر فرعون برشيد } حال من { فرعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rashīd derives from rashada and describes one who attains correctness.
rows.anchor: والرشيد : فعيل من رشد من باب نصر وفرح ، إذا اتصف بإصابة الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the command rashīd or not is a rational metaphor: the command is described by a quality properly belonging to its commander.
rows.anchor: وأجري وصف رشيد على الأمر مجازا عقليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is called lacking right guidance because it embodies the opposite of guidance so fully that it seems to possess the quality itself.
rows.anchor: مبالغة في اشتمال الأمر على ما يقتضي انتفاء الرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's command was folly, since there is no middle state between right guidance and folly.
rows.anchor: والمقصود أن أمر فرعون سفه إذ لا واسطة بين الرشد والسفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating guidance rather than directly calling the command foolish exposes the followers' irrationality: they followed something with no sign of soundness or merit.
rows.anchor: فماذا غرهم باتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about Pharaoh leading his people may be circumstantial to Pharaoh or a rhetorical explanatory resumption.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون في موضع الحال من { فرعون } ( هود : 97 ) المذكور في الجملة قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause may be an explanatory resumption.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون استئنافا بيانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īrād means to make something arrive at water; the leader who brings others there is called the fāriṭ or firṭ.
rows.anchor: والإيراد : جعل الشيء واردا ، أي قاصدا الماء ، والذي يوردهم هو الفارط ، ويقال له : الفرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wird, with kasra on wāw, is the water reached and is a faʿl form with passive-participial meaning, like dhabḥ.
rows.anchor: والورد بكسر الواو : الماء المورود ، وهو فعل بمعنى مفعول ، مثل دبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing Pharaoh's people to the Fire is a mocking metaphor for bringing people to water, normally done so they can benefit from drinking.
rows.anchor: استعارة الإيراد إلى التقدم بالناس إلى العذاب ، وهي تهكمية لأن الإيراد يكون لأجل الانتفاع بالسقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqdumu is the present of qadama, with fatḥa on dāl, meaning to go ahead of others and transitive when one precedes someone.
rows.anchor: و { يقدم } مضارع قدم بفتح الدال بمعنى تقدم المتعدي إذا كان متقدما غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past form fa-awradahum signals the certainty of the future leading, since the Resurrection setting shows it has not yet happened.
rows.anchor: للتنبيه على تحقيق وقوع ذلك الإيراد وإلا فقرينة قوله : { يوم القيامة } تدل على أنه لم يقع في الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause praising the terrible destination is circumstantial, with its deleted subject pronoun as the link; this strips away the metaphor because actual water is not blameworthy.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال والضمير المخصوص بالمدح المحذوف هو الرابط وهو تجريد للاستعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Itbāʿ means causing something to follow or attaching it afterward.
rows.anchor: والإتباع : الإلحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse is the curse of punishment in this world and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: واللعنة : هي لعنة العذاب في الدنيا وفي الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-qiyāmah modifies the act of following, so another curse follows them then; the first curse is already restricted to worldly life.
rows.anchor: فعلم أنهم أتبعوا لعنة يوم القيامة ، لأن اللعنة الأولى قيدت بالمجرور بحرف { في } الظرفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final condemnation is an independent sentence censuring the curse, with its omitted target inferred from the preceding mention of the curse.
rows.anchor: وجملة { بئس الرفد المرفود } مستأنفة لإنشاء ذم اللعنة . والمخصوص بالذم محذوف دل عليه ذكر اللعنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafd, with kasra on rāʾ, is a faʿl noun meaning what is given as aid; rafadah means giving helpful property or the like.
rows.anchor: والرفد بكسر الراء اسم على وزن فعل بمعنى مفعول مثل ذبح ، أي ما يرفد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the particular target of blame is concise and lets the censure apply indiscriminately to either curse, since both are evil.
rows.anchor: لأن كلتيهما بئيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a comprehensive closing summary and the surah's conclusion, an instance of rhetorical beauty at the ending.
rows.anchor: كلام جامع وهو تذييل للسورة مؤذن بختامها ، فهو من براعة المقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening wāw may connect one statement to another or function parenthetically, a common construction.
rows.anchor: والواو عاطفة كلاما على كلام ، أو واو الاعتراض في آخر الكلام ومثله كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām denotes ownership through comprehensive knowledge: God possesses what is unknown to people in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: واللام في { لله } للملك وهو ملك إحاطة العلم ، أي لله ما غاب عن علم الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen promises believers hidden bliss and warns polytheists of punishment hidden from them in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: بشارة المؤمنين بما وعدوا من النعيم المغيب عنهم ، ونذارة المشركين بما توعدوا به من العذاب المغيب عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting both phrases conveys exclusivity: only God owns knowledge of the unseen and only to Him does every matter return.
rows.anchor: تقديم المجرورين في { ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وإليه يرجع الأمر } لإفادة الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This exclusivity rebuts worship of others: one without these attributes does not deserve worship, while the one possessing them deserves worship alone.
rows.anchor: لأن من لم يكن كذلك لا يستحق أن يعبد ، ومن كان كذلك كان حقيقا بأن يفرد بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All affairs returning to God means governance, victory, defeat, and similar outcomes ultimately depend on His knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: أن أمر التدبير والنصر والخذلان وغير ذلك يرجع إلى الله ، أي إلى علمه وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human preparations often fail: the powerful may be humbled unexpectedly, while the weak may gain strength and victory over the mighty.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا ما اعتز العزيز بعزته فلقي الخذلان من حيث لا يرتقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-amr is definite as a generic noun and so covers affairs generally; kulluhu explicitly makes the totality clear.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { الأمر } تعريف الجنس فيعم الأمور ، وتأكيد الأمر ب { كله } للتنصيص على العموم

rows.speaker: من عدا نافعا
rows.claim: All reciters except Nāfiʿ read yarjiʿ in the passive: every holder of an affair has that affair returned to God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ من عدا نافعا { يرجع } ببناء الفعل بصيغة النائب

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads yarjiʿ in the active, making al-amr the subject: the affair itself returns to God.
rows.anchor: وقرأه نافع بصيغة الفاعل على أن يكون ( الأمر ) هو فاعل الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either reading, return pictures humans' inability to control affairs as someone who handles an object but must hand it back to its proper controller.
rows.anchor: تمثيل لهيئة عجز الناس عن التصرف في الأمور حسب رغباتهم بهيئة متناول شيء للتصرف به ثم عدم استطاعته التصرف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it pictures affairs submitting to God's control as a traveler seeking a resting place and finally returning to its proper abode; this is an implicit representational metaphor signaled by yarjiʿ and ilayhi.
rows.anchor: فهي تمثيلية مكنية رمز إليها بفعل { يرجع } وتعديته ب { إليه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship and rely on God follows because He alone deserves worship and trust; it rebukes worship of others and reliance on idols' intercession, and commands the Prophet's continued devotion.
rows.anchor: لأن الله هو الحقيق بأن يعبد وأن يتوكل عليه في كل مهم . وهو تعريض بالتخطئة للذين عبدوا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended command is to worship and rely on God alone, inferred from the return of every affair to Him and the logic of the command, so explicit restrictive wording is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: والمراد أن يعبده دون غيره ويتوكل عليه دون غيره بقرينة { وإليه يرجع الأمر كله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final statement that God is not heedless is a comprehensive conclusion to what precedes; its wāw functions like the opening wāw.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون } فذلكة جامعة ، فهو تذييل لما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's not overlooking deeds means every doer receives the corresponding recompense, good for good and evil for evil; linking heedlessness to deeds signals their consequences.
rows.anchor: يعطي كل عامل جزاء عمله إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر

rows.speaker: نافع ، وابن عامر ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وأبو جعفر ، ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers use the second-person plural taʿmalūn, addressing the Prophet and the people with him.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وابن عامر ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وأبو جعفر ، ويعقوب ( عما تعملون ) بتاء فوقية خطابا للنبيء

rows.speaker: من عداهم
rows.claim: The remaining readers use third-person yaʿmalūn, referring to the unbelievers and thereby consoling the Prophet while warning the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقرأ من عداهم بالمثناة التحتية على أن يعود الضمير إلى الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-shahādah is a verbal noun used with passive meaning for things witnessed: visible objects and other perceptible things, thus joining the unseen and witnessed into all existence.
rows.anchor: فهي هنا مصدر بمعنى المفعول ، أي الأشياء المشهودة ، وهي الظاهرة المحسوسة ، المرئيات وغيرها من المحسوسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kabīr metaphorically denotes greatness; language of size and multitude became conventional for majesty through comparing abstract meaning to sensory magnitude.
rows.anchor: والكبير : مجاز في العظمة ، إذ قد شاع استعمال أسماء الكثرة وألفاظ الكبر في العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mutaʿāl means exalted; its tafaʿul form marks elevation as an inherent attribute, necessary in itself rather than conferred by another.
rows.anchor: والمتعالي : المترفع . وصيغت الصفة بصيغة التفاعل للدلالة على أن العلو صفة ذاتية له لا من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exaltation means either complete invincibility, beyond any being's power to overcome or compel, or transcendence above deficiencies.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالرفعة هنا المجاز عن العزة التامة بحيث لا يستطيع موجود أن يغلبه أو يكرهه ، أو المنزه عن النقائص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final yāʾ in al-mutaʿāl is omitted to fit the verse endings, including the cadence shared with wāl and al-āṣāl.
rows.anchor: وحذف الياء من المتعال } لمرعاة الفواصل الساكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh says yāʾs and wāws normally preferred in form may be dropped in verse endings and rhyme; retaining them is more analogical, while deletion is common Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر سيبويه أن ما يختار إثباته من الياءات والواوات يحذف في الفواصل والقوافي ، والإثبات أقيس والحذف عربي كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the successive guardians may attach to the relative pronoun in the preceding verse, as a second predicate about all the people described there.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون متصلة ب { من } الموصولة من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that construction, singular pronouns refer individually to each person in the listed categories, all alike in God's knowledge, each guarded through the relevant periods.
rows.anchor: جاءت مفردة لأن كلا منها عائد إلى أحد أصحاب تلك الصلات حيث إن ذكرهم ذكر أقسام من الذين جعلوا سواء في علم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively the clause may attach only to the hidden person and daytime traveler, with singular pronouns preserving the coordination of relative clauses without repeating the relative pronoun; the sense is the same.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تتصل الجملة ب { من هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muʿaqqibāt is the feminine active participle plural of ʿaqqaba, to follow; its intensive pattern evokes following someone as if stepping on his heel, and the intended beings are angels.
rows.anchor: و ( المعقبات ) جمع معقبة بفتح العين وتشديد القاف مكسورة اسم فاعل عقبه إذا تبعه . وصيغة التفعيل فيه للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word derives from ʿaqab, heel, and the singular is muʿaqqib.
rows.anchor: والمراد : ملائكة معقبات . والواحد معقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine plural form treats the guardians as groups.
rows.anchor: وإنما جمع جمع مؤنث بتأويل الجماعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥifẓ means surveillance, as in naming the watcher a ḥafīẓ; the angels watch each person in secrecy and openness, stillness and movement.
rows.anchor: والحفظ : المراقبة ، ومنه سمي الرقيب حفيظا . والمعنى : يراقبون كل أحد في أحواله من إسرار وإعلان ، وسكون وحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between his hands and behind him means surrounding him from every direction.
rows.anchor: و { من بين يديه ومن خلفه } مستعمل في معنى الإحاطة من الجهات كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min amr Allāh may describe the guardians as groups from God's troops and command, as in the cited verses where spirit is from God's command and means the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: صفة { معقبات } ، أي جماعات من جند الله وأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the guardians protect hidden people at night and travelers by day from thieves, venomous creatures, crowds, and fighting; min amr Allāh then depends on yaḥfaẓūnahu and means protection from God's creatures.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الحفظ على الوجه الثاني مرادا به الوقاية والصيانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This protection is a favor: without God's kindness even the smallest thing could harm people.
rows.anchor: وهذا منة على العباد بلطف الله بهم وإلا لكان أدنى شيء يضر بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is parenthetical between proof of God's power and knowledge in creation and the reminder about His power in the next verse.
rows.anchor: جملة معترضة بين الجمل المتقدمة المسوقة للاستدلال على عظيم قدرة الله تعالى وعلمه بمصنوعاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It warns them against persistence in idolatry by warning of worldly punishment, since they demanded evil before good while enjoying prosperity, acting arrogantly, mocking the Messenger, and belittling believers.
rows.anchor: والمقصود تحذيرهم من الإصرار على الشرك بتحذيرهم من حلول العقاب في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds them that their prosperity can be removed because of their bad deeds after they have been warned and invited to faith.
rows.anchor: فذكرهم الله بنعمته عليهم ونبههم إلى أن زوالها لا يكون إلا بسبب أعمالهم السيئة بعد ما أنذرهم ودعاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing means replacement by something different; the warning tells prosperous polytheists that they have exposed their blessings to change.
rows.anchor: والتغيير : التبديل بالمغاير ، فلا جرم أنه تديد لأولي النعمة من المشركين بأنهم قد تعرضوا لتغييرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative mā denotes a state, the bāʾ means attachment, and the state meant is a people's blessing; changing other states can be desirable.
rows.anchor: الموصولة حالة ، والباء للملابسة ، أي حالة ملابسة لقوم ، أي حالة نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing what people have is attributed to them as a rational metaphor for their causing it through their own conduct.
rows.anchor: وأطلق التغيير في قوله : { حتى يغيروا } على التسبب فيه على طريقة المجاز العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that no one can repel God's will explicitly restates the implication of the until-clause and intensifies the warning, since fear calls for directness.
rows.anchor: تصريح بمفهوم الغاية المستفاد من { حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم } تأكيدا للتحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills to change a people's condition as they change themselves, nothing can resist His decision; they must not presume they can wait for punishment and then believe.
rows.anchor: وذلك تحذير من الغرور أن يقولوا : سنسترسل على ما نحن فيه فإذا رأينا العذاب آمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of any protector besides God further warns against imagining that idols will intercede for them.
rows.anchor: زيادة في التحذير من الغرور لئلا يحسبوا أن أصنامهم شفعاؤهم عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wālī means one who manages another's affairs through planning and benefit, from the root for nearness in the sense of close involvement.
rows.anchor: والوالي : الذي يلي أمر أحد ، أي يشتغل بأمره اشتغال تدبير ونفع ، مشتق من ولي إذا قرب

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read wāl with tanwīn and omit its yāʾ in both connected recitation and pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { من وال } بتنوين { وال } دون ياء في الوصل والوقف

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains the yāʾ after lām only when pausing, omitting it in connected reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير بياء بعد اللام وقفا فقط دون الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parenthetical resumption contrasts those led astray with the guided and shows that believers' hearts rest with God's remembrance, while the demand for a sign showed the others did not count the Qur'an as God's sign.
rows.anchor: مناسبته المضادة لحال الذين أضلهم الله ، والبيان لحال الذين هداهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning believers' reward here both states their outcome and implies the opposite outcome for the previous group, while pointing to the causes of each.
rows.anchor: فذكرها عقب الجملة السابقة يفيد الغرضين ويشير إلى السببين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first alladhīna āmanū is the subject; the reassurance sentence is parenthetical; the second alladhīna āmanū is an exact apposition, and ṭūbā lahum is the predicate.
rows.anchor: ف { الذين آمنوا } الأول مبتدأ ، وجملة { ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب } معترضة و { الذين آمنوا } الثاني بدل مطابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṭmiʾnān literally means stillness, used here for certainty and absence of doubt, since doubt is metaphorically agitation.
rows.anchor: والاطمئنان : السكون ، واستعير هنا لليقين وعدم الشك ، لأن الشك يستعار له الاضطراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr Allāh may mean fearing and remembering God by observing His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يراد به خشية الله ومراقبته بالوقوف عند أمره ونهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr may mean the Qur'an, fitting the demand for a sign; Qur'an is called a reminder, and other verses describe hearts hardened or softened by it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد به القرآن قال : وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it can mean remembering God aloud, since reciting God's name awakens hearts to His watchfulness.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد ذكر الله باللسان فإن إجراءه على اللسان ينبه القلوب إلى مراقبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes believers' good state against disbelievers whose hearts are submerged in doubt.
rows.anchor: وهذا وصف لحسن حال المؤمنين ومقايسته بسوء حالة الكافرين الذين غمر الشك قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This answers the demand for a sign: the earlier reply about God leading whom He wills dismissed their ignorance, while this passage directly rebuts their claim; it may be spoken after qul or stand independently.
rows.anchor: هذا الجواب عن قولهم : { لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه } لأن الجواب السابق بقوله : { قل إن الله يضل من يشاء } جواب بالإعراض عن جهالتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening kadhālika points back emphatically to the amazement at their error in failing to recognize the Messenger's status.
rows.anchor: وفي افتتاحها بقوله : { كذلك } الذي هو اسم إشارة تأكيد للمشار إليه وهو التعجب من ضلالتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to sending itself: He sent the Prophet in a sending so clear that it resembles itself and needs no explanation.
rows.anchor: فالمشبه به عين المشبه ، إشارة إلى أنه لوضوحه لا يبين ما وضح من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Prophet is sent to a community after earlier communities, his mission resembles theirs; this rebuts the notion that lacking requested signs means he is not God's messenger and prepares for the next verse.
rows.anchor: أي ما كانت رسالتك إلا مثل رسالة الرسل من قبلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummah here means the community to whom the message is addressed, some of whom believe and some disbelieve.
rows.anchor: والأمة : هي أمة الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of earlier communities indirectly warns of the fate of nations that rejected their messengers.
rows.anchor: ويتضمن قوله : قد خلت من قبلها أمم } التعريض بالوعيد بمثل مصير الأمم الخالية التي كذبت رسلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose lām in li-tatlu shows that the mission aims to guide people by God's instruction, not to perform wonders for their own sake.
rows.anchor: أن الإرسال لأجل الإرشاد والهداية بما أمر الله لا لأجل الانتصاب لخوارق العادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilāwah means reading: the purpose is to recite the Qur'an to them.
rows.anchor: والتلاوة : القراءة . فالمقصود لتقرأ عليهم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This implies that the Qur'an is the Prophet's miracle, as it is set against earlier prophets' missions and the demand for a sign; another verse states this explicitly.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيماء إلى أن القرآن هو معجزته

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said each prophet was given signs of the kind that people believed through, whereas his own gift was revelation from God.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي : ما من الأنبياء نبي إلا أوتي من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that they disbelieve in al-Raḥmān is coordinated with the sending statement; its pronoun refers to the contextually understood polytheists, not the whole community, which also contains believers.
rows.anchor: فالضمير عائد إلى المشركين المفهومين من المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense yakfurūn indicates that their disbelief is renewed and continuing.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالمضارع في { يكفرون } للدلالة على تجدد ذلك واستمراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disbelief in God consists in associating another with Him in divinity, thereby negating what divinity truly means.
rows.anchor: ومعنى كفرهم بالله إشراكهم معه غيره في الإلهية ، فقد أبطلوا حقيقة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān is singled out because they denied that name, as when they asked who the Merciful was; it also fits the Messenger and Qur'an as guidance and mercy, unlike wonders that only attest a messenger.
rows.anchor: واختيار اسم ( الرحمن ) من بين أسمائه تعالى لأن كفرهم بهذا الاسم أشد لأنهم أنكروا أن يكون الله رحمان

rows.speaker: مقاتل وابن جريج
rows.claim: They report that the verse came at Hudaybiyyah: Suhayl ibn ʿAmr objected to writing In the name of the Merciful, saying they knew al-Raḥmān only as Musaylimah of Yamāmah, so the Prophet had the scribe write In Your name, O God.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل وابن جريج : نزلت هذه الآية في صلح الحديبية حين أرادوا أن يكتبوا كتاب الصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr considers the Hudaybiyyah report unlikely because this surah is Meccan.
rows.anchor: ويبعده أن السورة مكية كما تقدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the verse was revealed about Quraysh unbelievers who, when told to prostrate to al-Raḥmān, asked who the Merciful was.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس نزلت في كفار قريش حين قال لهم النبي اسجدوا للرحمن قالوا وما الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God instructs the Prophet to answer that al-Raḥmān is his Lord; the pronoun refers to the person named by al-Raḥmān, identifying that name with his Lord.
rows.anchor: فضمير { هو } عائد إلى ( الرحمن ) باعتبار المسمى بهذا الاسم ، أي المسمى هو ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La ilāha illā huwa refutes associating other gods with God; it is part of the commanded reply, showing the one invoked as al-Raḥmān is the same one invoked as Allah, not a parenthetical divine statement.
rows.anchor: فكان قوله : { لا إلاه إلا هو } دالا على أن المدعو بالرحمان هو المدعو بالله إذ لا إلاه إلا إلاه واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reliance on God and return to Him follow from His being the sole Lord; the connected consequence is set apart because the two statements are closely linked.
rows.anchor: وجملة { عليه توكلت وإليه متاب } هي نتيجة لكونه ربا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting عليه and إليه gives exclusive reliance and repentance: the one God is trusted, and His mercy makes Him the fitting recipient of repentance.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المجرورين وهما { عليه } و { إليه } لإفادة اختصاص التوكل والمتاب بالكون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāb is an emphatic mīmī verbal noun meaning repentance, originally a time noun figuratively used for the action and then lexicalized as a direct noun.
rows.anchor: والمتاب : مصدر ميمي على وزن مفعل ، أي التوبة ، يفيد المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because matāb conveys returning to God's commands, it takes ilā; its original possessive final yāʾ was dropped for ease, with the kasra retained as its trace.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المتاب متضمنا معنى الرجوع إلى ما يأمر الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After answering denials that the Qur'an comes from God, the passage gives Moses as a parallel: he was sent like Muhammad and to bring his people from darkness into light.
rows.anchor: أعقب الرد بالتمثيل بالنظير وهو إرسال موسى عليه السلام إلى قومه بمثل ما أرسل به محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath lām and qad reinforce Moses's sending because deniers of Muhammad's mission are treated as if denying Moses's too; what applies to the like applies to its counterpart, and some had claimed God sent no human revelation.
rows.anchor: لتنزيل المنكرين رسالة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم منزلة من ينكر رسالة موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in bi-āyātinā marks accompaniment: Moses was sent with signs of his truth, just as Muhammad was accompanied by the Qur'an, completing the analogy and proof.
rows.anchor: إرسالا مصاحبا للآيات الدالة على صدقه في رسالته ، كما أرسل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم مصاحبا لآية القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is explanatory: it explicates the sending through the command to bring his people out, since sending includes the meaning of saying.
rows.anchor: و { أن } تفسيرية ، فسر الإرسال بجملة ( أخرج قومك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness is a metaphor for associationism and sins, and light for true faith and piety.
rows.anchor: و { الظلمات } مستعار للشرك والمعاصي ، و { النور } مستعار للإيمان الحق والتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Joseph's death the Israelites spent a long time in Egypt, adopted Egyptian polytheism, and needed Moses both to reform belief and invite Pharaoh's people to monotheism; his mission was to move them into faith and righteousness.
rows.anchor: لما طال عليهم الأمد في مصر بعد وفاة يوسف عليه السلام سرى إليهم الشرك واتبعوا دين القبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminder removes forgetfulness and can teach what people should already know; because it carries warning and exhortation, it takes bāʾ, meaning an admonishing reminder of God's days.
rows.anchor: ولما ضمن التذكير معنى الإنذار والوعظ عدي بالباء ، أي ذكرهم تذكير عظة بأيام الله
